thread:
michelle: Hey team — customer (org: AcmeRetail) seeing lots of 429s during peak yesterday. They say they have a single API key but are behind a NATed proxy with many clients.  Request ID samples: rid=01H8X2...; logs show 429s with message 'quota_exhausted'. Billing didn't spike but user-facing errors did. Can we triage?

raj: Thanks — can you paste one raw request header set from the failing client? specifically looking for Authorization + any X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP headers.

michelle: Pasted below from customer capture (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***
Host: api.redwood.example
User-Agent: AcmeClient/2.1
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.1.45, 34.120.5.8
X-Request-Id: 01H8X2ABC
```
They also said sometimes requests come without X-Forwarded-For (proxy strips it intermittently).

karen: TL;DR likely scoping mismatch: when both API key and IP are present we evaluate quota scoping priority. If X-Forwarded-For missing we use egress IP which groups many users -> org-level or IP-based quota might be hit. Do we have a concrete repro?

dylan: Checked telemetry for those request IDs — interesting: the token bound quota shows usage under key-level limits, but the enforcement decision logged `active_scope=org` for several hits. Looks like the attribution pipeline sometimes prefers org/project scope over key when token metadata is stale. Suspect race in auth cache TTL.

michelle: Repro steps customer provided: 1) spin many clients behind a single NAT; 2) rotate keys rapidly (they rotate every 5m); 3) occasionally drop X-Forwarded-For header. They see burst 429s after rotation.

raj: That rotation + missing forwarded header + cache TTL could lead to temporary loss of key->project mapping, so requests fall back to org or ip fingerprint. Two asks: (1) can SRE pull auth cache logs for these rid timestamps, (2) can we run a small repro here with curl loop to validate behavior?

sre-bot: Incident note created: #INC-2024-524 — assigned to oncall infra. Uploading auth-cache traces for 1729805432..1729805600.

dylan: Quick mitigation idea: if auth mapping TTL expired we should prefer explicit Authorization header mapping to API-key scope before considering IP/org heuristics. I can sketch a safe-change rollback: check header-based mapping first, then fallback to ip/org. Would that break any existing quota semantics (esp. org-level caps)?

karen: That would tighten key isolation which customers expect. Risk: some customers rely on IP fallback for legacy billing mappings; but default should prioritize credential identity. I support a patch that makes header precedence explicit with a feature flag for a week rollout.

michelle: Customer asked for short-term workaround — can we recommend they: a) ensure X-Forwarded-For is preserved, b) stop rotating keys so frequently while we investigate, or c) request a temporary dedicated capacity bump?

raj: Yes to those. Also can we add server-side telemetry tag when we enforce ip/org fallback so support teams can filter faster? Add `enforcement_reason=ip_fallback` to logs.

michelle: Noted. I'll reply to customer with the mitigations and ask for a small curl script to reproduce. If they can share a short capture (10s) we'll run it in staging.

dylan: I'll prototype the header-first auth fix and a unit test covering key rotation + missing XFF case. Will post PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

michelle: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread updated. If we see more org-level 429s we escalate to infra-oncall.
